subject: [PATCH 2/3] blk-iocost: clear delay state when freeing policy data

reviews.author: Sashiko
reviews.summary: Raised a high-severity concern that the unconditional call to blkcg_clear_delay() might overwrite state managed by other active policies like blk-iolatency, and suggested checking if iocost had actually set a delay before clearing it.

2026-08-06.patch_summary: This patch series addresses issues in the blk-iocost policy by clearing delay state when freeing policy data and handling debt accumulation. The first patch fixes a double-put bug in fuse_try_move_page() where the folio refcount drops to zero prematurely, while the second patch clears the delay state explicitly after removing the iocg from active_iocgs and cancelling its waitq timer.

reviews.author: Tejun Heo
reviews.summary: Confirmed that the two mechanisms aren't usually used together and even when they step on each other, use_delay being cleared spuriously is transient and nothing really breaks.
reviews.raw_body:
> Does this unconditional call to blkcg_clear_delay() overwrite state managed
> by other policies?
> 
> Since use_delay is shared among block cgroup policies, if iocost never
> actually applied a delay, this might forcefully zero out the delay state
> managed by other active policies like blk-iolatency. 
> 
> Would it be safer to check if iocost had actually set a delay before clearing
> it here?

Yeah, this is fine. The two mechanisms aren't usually used together and even
when they step on each other, use_delay being cleared spuriously is
transient and nothing really breaks.

Thanks.

-- 
tejun
